references.note: The sower scatters seed, while growth proceeds beyond his full understanding through successive stages until harvest. Compare the balance of action, patience, and recognition of ripeness with the compilation’s images of cultivation. The parable concerns the kingdom of God; its agricultural image offers a way to think about growth without setting a timetable for every social or spiritual change.

subjects.displayTitle: Unity of existence: what does oneness mean?
subjects.introduction: All the saplings of the world have grown from one Tree, Bahá’u’lláh writes, and every drop belongs to one Ocean. To say that existence is one sounds simple until one asks what kind of oneness is meant. The Sufis pictured God as the sea and creatures as its waves, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá honours what they were reaching for while refusing the picture: the Pre-existent does not descend into the contingent, nor does absolute wealth take on poverty. His own image is the sun, whose rays light everything without the sun leaving its place. The Báb presses the point harder still, and Bahá’u’lláh finds another unity in the wayfarer who forgets self so completely that nothing remains but the Friend. The dependence of all things on one source, the many powers of a single soul, the creation in which all things are involved in all things: these meanings touch without collapsing into each other. Plotinus, describing how the One produces what proceeds from it while remaining itself, offers the classical counterpart [1]. From here the inquiry opens onto God’s oneness in its two stations, the uncompounded reality, the interconnectedness of beings, and the question of pantheism.
subjects.arc: Begin with dependence and distinction, examine the philosophical debate, then compare unity in the soul, the world, and spiritual experience.

order.why: Examine manifestation and emanation through seed and sun.
shortened: The difference resides in the fact that the Sufis maintain that the realities of all things are the manifestation of the One, whereas the Prophets say that they emanate therefrom. And great indeed is the difference between manifestation and emanation. Appearance through manifestation means that a single thing becomes manifest in infinite forms. For example, when the seed, which is a single thing endowed with the perfections of the vegetable kingdom, manifests itself, it becomes resolved into the infinite forms of the branches, leaves, flowers, and fruit. This is called manifestational appearance, whereas in appearance through emanation the One remains transcendent in the heights of its sanctity, but the existence of the creatures is obtained from it through emanation, not manifestation. It can be compared to the sun: The rays emanate from it and shine forth upon all things, but the sun remains transcendent in the heights of its sanctity.

order.why: Open with the trees, drops and beings dependent upon one source.
Distinguish oneness from simply calling several things identical.
Read the careful explanation of what leading Sufi thinkers intended.
shortened: Rather, what these pre-eminent figures have alluded to is an existence compared to which the realities of all things are mere accidents. By this is intended an existence that is pre-eternal whilst all other things are contingent. Thus, the existence to which they refer is that ineffable Reality whereby all things are realized, or, in other words, by virtue of which all things subsist, but which itself remaineth self-subsistent above the heavens and the earth.

order.why: Consider relative nothingness before the divine presence.
Read the account of philosophical and mystical formulations.
shortened: Likewise have the mystics put forth statements concerning unity and the explanation of the station of abstraction. In this regard, he who was their exemplar among those who spoke of the unity of existence, and their model among those who affirmed the vision of Truth in every existing thing, hath said that the outward aspect of the Lord cannot be numbered and His inward aspect cannot be limited, that the outward can scarce be manifest and the inward can scarce be concealed. Many have followed him in this, likening this station to the sea and its waves, to ink and letters, to water and ice.

order.why: Examine the criticism of the ocean and wave analogy.
shortened: However, the mystics imagine that this existence is like an ocean and all beings are like its waves. This metaphor and expression is deficient, for if you look at reality, it would necessitate that the Pre-existent descend to the realm of the contingent, the Absolute Rich take on the form of poverty, Pure Being adorn itself with non-existence, and Divine Light assume the form of worldly darkness. In short, in their view existence is limited to the Truth and creation with no third between them - its inner reality is the Truth, its outer form creation; the reality is the ocean and the form is the wave.

order.why: Keep the reported account of the birds and the contrast concerning mediation.
shortened: Another celebrated poet "Attar" portrays this idea of pantheism in a long wonderful poem called the "Parliament of birds. The poem is written allegorically. It is said that "Hodhod," a very beautiful bird came one day to all the other birds and said, let us all gather together and make a pilgrimage to the Mountain of "Qaff" - where the King of birds "Seymorg" dwells on a lofty peak. (Now "Seymorg" is a fabulous, mythical bird in the ancient literature of Persia but it means literally 30 birds; "Sey" means 30, "Morg," bird.) Then "Hodhod" sent out messengers to all parts of the world to announce the approaching departure of the birds for the Mountain of "Qaff." Millions of birds joined the Caravan. At last they were ready and started on their long journey. They had to cross many waste deserts and many desolated valleys. They flew over many high mountains. For days they could get neither food nor water. Consequently many of them died on the way. The rays of the Sun burned and scorched the wings and feathers of many thousand and they fell on the desert strewing the trail with their dead bodies. Finally the large army was woefully decimated and only "30 birds" reached the mountain of "Qaff." Having attained to the summit, they did not find any "Seymorg" but looking around they saw they are "Seymorg" themselves.

But the Baha'is say there is God, the creatures and the medium. They state that the Reality of Divinity is Absolute Independence; if it comes within the circle of necessity, It is not Divinity; the Reality of Divinity is Absolute Perfection but the creatures are pure imperfection. Consequently there are channels between God and man. These channels are the Holy Divine Manifestations.

order.why: Read the Báb’s argument about divine knowledge and its objects.
shortened: And since it hath been established that His Essence is His Life -- and Life, in itself, requireth not the existence of any other living thing -- so likewise is the decree concerning Knowledge: glorified be He! He was, in the pre-eternity of pre-eternities, All-Knowing, without the existence of an object known.

order.why: Preserve the Báb’s forceful critique of unity and causation.
shortened: Those who claim the unity of existence are polytheists, by the testimony of existence itself, for the unity they affirm is contingent upon the existence of two, else from what station would come the negation of two and affirmation of unity?

Rather, the True Reality is the Essence of Truth. Creation is contingent, and nothing beyond contingent creation is conceivable. Truth has ever been Truth, and no thing is known. Creation will ever be creation, and connection with the Essence is impossible.

order.why: Hear the Báb’s distinction between seeing divine command and creation.
Keep the statement concerning the indivisible source.
shortened: All things return unto this Indivisible One Being (shay'-I-vahid), and all things are created by this Indivisible One Being.

order.why: Read the signs of oneness throughout things.
shortened: Thus the signs of oneness are manifest and evident in all things. How much more is the Creator of all things!

order.why: Consider unity in the language of might and mercy.
Describes the interrelation and transformation of beings throughout existence.
Read waves, shadows and earth as invitations to recognize their source.
Return from plurality toward the source of number.
shortened: How many floods have overflowed, and how many rivers have sprung forth and flowed, yet all draw their sustenance from the mighty ocean. Return therefore from the world of pluralities to unity, and from numbers to the One which is the source of all numbers. That One is sanctified beyond the limitation of the unifiers.

order.why: Introduce the rational soul through its varied powers.
Read one reality expressing itself through different instruments.
shortened: Say: Spirit, mind, soul, and the powers of sight and hearing are but one single reality which hath manifold expressions owing to the diversity of its instruments. As thou dost observe, man's power to comprehend, move, speak, hear, and see all derive from this sign of his Lord within him. It is single in its essence, yet manifold through the diversity of its instruments. This, verily, is a certain truth. For example, if it directeth its attention to the means of hearing, then hearing and its attributes become manifest.

order.why: Compare the Forel Tablet’s soul, faculties and mirror.
Hear the reported use of different names for one human reality.
shortened: It is the same reality which is given different names, according to the different conditions wherein it becomes manifest. Because of its attachment to matter and the phenomenal world, when it governs the physical functions of the body it is called the human soul. When it manifests itself as the thinker, the comprehender, it is called the mind. And when it soars into the atmosphere of God, and travels in the spiritual world, it becomes designated as spirit.

order.why: Read the further reported distinction of names according to function.
Consider one essence described at different stages.
Keep the reported rejection of the soul’s absorption like a drop in the sea.
Read one world apprehended through different grades of reality.
shortened: Now the greatest doubt of the deniers is this: where is that world? And everything which has no concrete external existence is mere imagination. However, the world of existence is one world, but it becomes manifold in relation to diverse realities. For example, the mineral, vegetable and animal worlds are one world, but the animal world in relation to the vegetable world is a spiritual reality and another realm, another condition.

order.why: Consider the reported movement of a material element through different forms.
shortened: As each component atom or element in the physical organisms of existence is subject to transference through endless forms and stages, possessing virtues peculiar to those forms and stations, it is evident that all phenomena of material being are fundamentally one. In the mineral kingdom this component atom or element possesses certain virtues of the mineral; in the kingdom of the vegetable it is imbued with vegetable qualities or virtues; in the plane of animal existence it is empowered with animal virtues -- the senses; and in the kingdom of man it manifests qualities peculiar to the human station.

order.why: Read the reported elemental account of oneness and pantheism.
Hear the brief reported statement about nature and expression.
shortened: Nature manifests in various forms, but the basic element is the same. There is unity of essence and variety of expression.

order.why: Keep the reported distinction of existence as it appears in different grades.
Consider the reported interdependence of beings as one great person.
Read the reported analogy of unity and numbers.
Consider the reported relation of reality and its focal expression.
Keep the reported image of reflection through a polished mirror.
Read the language of unity within its context of the hidden craft.
Consider the imagery of separation and reunion within the source’s account of craftsmanship.
Enter the Seven Valleys’ account of unity and self-forgetfulness.
shortened: 35 After passing through the Valley of Knowledge, which is the last station of limitation, the wayfarer cometh to the FIRST STATION OF UNITY and drinketh from the cup of oneness, and gazeth upon the manifestations of singleness. In this station he pierceth the veils of plurality, fleeth the realms of the flesh, and ascendeth unto the heaven of unity.

This station is that of dying to the self and living in God, of being poor in self and rich in the Desired One. Poverty, as here referred to, signifieth being poor in that which pertaineth to the world of creation and rich in what belongeth to the realms of God. For when the true lover and devoted friend reacheth the presence of the Beloved, the radiant beauty of the Loved One and the fire of the lover's heart will kindle a blaze and burn away all veils and wrappings. Yea, all that he hath, from marrow to skin, will be set aflame, so that nothing will remain save the Friend.

order.why: Read the wish that limited selfhood’s veils pass away.
Close the linked passages with finding all through finding God.
Retain the supplied Plotinus passage as a philosophical comparison.
Hear the supplied Heraclitus fragment concerning the account of unity.
Read the supplied Vedic statement of one reality and many names.
Read the supplied distinction between unconscious obedience and discerning faith.
shortened: Know that faith is of two kinds. The first is objective faith that is expressed by the outer man, obedience of the limbs and senses. The other faith is subjective, and unconscious obedience to the will of God.

This condition of unconscious obedience constitutes subjective faith. But the discerning faith that consists of true knowledge of God and the comprehension of divine words, of such faith there is very little in any age. That is why His Holiness Christ said to His followers, "Many are called but few are chosen."

order.why: Keep the supplied scholarly interpretation of the Báb’s writings.
Consider the supplied letter about the soul and its divine reflection.
shortened: All these terms are different ways of referring to the one great reality within man, that divine spark of Reality which is the secret of his superiority over the rest of creation. That Divine Spark of Reality is in the nature of a reflection of the Divine Attributes in man, just as the mirror reflects the light of the sun.

order.why: Read the supplied account of different modes of knowing.
Compare the supplied Ghazálí passage on names and meanings.
Keep the supplied Plotinus passage on the soul’s many powers.
Read the supplied provisional account of one reality in diverse actions.
Retain the supplied provisional explanation of two stations of unity.
shortened: Two stations can be observed in the Divine Unity: Existential Oneness (tawhid-i wujudi), and this is that [station] wherein they negate everything with a 'no' and affirm the Absolute Reality. This means that they do not acknowledge the existence of anything other than the Absolute Reality, in the sense that all things, when placed next to the manifestation and remembrance of It, have been and will continue to be absolute nothingness (fana-yi mahd). 'All things perish save the [Divine] face'.... [The second station in Divine Unity,] Manifestational Oneness (tawhid-i shuhudi), is that [station] where the signs of the Primal Divine Unity (ahadiyah), the manifestations of Eternity, and the effulgences of the light of Singleness can be observed in all things.

The meaning of the philosopher was not that the Absolute Reality is dispersed into the innumerable existent things. Exalted, exalted is It from being dispersed in anything or being limited by any boundary or being associated with anything in creation.

order.why: Preserve the supplied provisional critique with its interpretive note.
shortened: Most of the Islamic philosophers, the peripatetic philosophers, the followers of Mulla Sadra (as-Sadra'iyyin), and the Theosophical philosophers (al-ilahiyyin) have erred in their explanations of this station.

Thus they went along with erroneous statements concerning the Eternal Archetypes (a`yan thabita) being in the Essence [of God] in order to establish His knowledge (praised be He)[1]; and with mention of the Uncompounded Reality in order to establish causality (`illiyya) in the Essence [of God]; and with mention of the connection between the Essence [of God] and [His] actions and attributes; and with the mention of the oneness of Being (wahdat al-wujud) between the Creator (mujid) and the one who has gone astray (al-mafqud). All of this is absolute heresy (shirk mahd) in the estimation of the family of God, the Imams of justice, for God has always been the All-Knowing without the existence of anything having form and shape (? - shay'un bi-mithl ma inna-hu kana shayyar).

order.why: Read the supplied scholarly account of stages in a philosophy of unity.
shortened: The wahidiyah, is the ontological state at which the original absolute Oneness of the reality of existence appears with inner articulations. These inner articulations are called, in accordance with the traditional terminology of theology, divine Names and Attributes. In this sense the stage of wahidiyah is called the stage of the Names and Attributes (asma' wa-sifat). Another name of this stage is the stage of knowledge (`ilm), i.e. divine Consciousness. This appellation comes from the idea that the wahidiyah is the stage at which God becomes conscious of Himself in the form of His own essential Perfections (kamalat dhatiyah). The essential Perfections of God that are thus established in divine Consciousness with clear demarcations are called the 'eternal Archetypes' (a`yan thabitah).

The eternal Archetypes are to be regarded as ontological models which are eternally established in divine Consciousness and upon which the phenomenal things are produced in the empirical dimension of time and space....

order.why: Close with the supplied Shaykh Ahmad passage as a further, distinct argument.
shortened: The notion of the unity of the thinker with the object of thought is based upon what was put forward by the author of the doctrine of the oneness of existence (wahdat al-wujud). He was obliged, for the sake of the correctness of this principle, to forget what it implied in corruption of belief and to cross over into unworthy speculations. God willing, we will explain the falsity of everything he depends upon and the repugnance of what he implies, such as the oneness of the agent and the patient, cause and effect, and so on....

questions: What different meanings of oneness can you identify in these passages?
How does the distinction between emanation and manifestation change what the sun or seed analogy explains?
Where does an image such as ocean and waves illuminate the inquiry, and where do the texts challenge it?
How does the unity of a person’s powers differ from the unity of all existence?
What similarities and differences emerge when Plotinus’s One is read beside the arguments here?
How might attention to these distinctions influence the way you approach both mystical experience and other philosophical traditions?

references.label: 1 · Plotinus, Enneads V.2.1–2 · The source and what proceeds from it
references.note: Read the Second Tractate of the Fifth Ennead in the MacKenna and Page translation. Plotinus describes the One’s production of Intellect and Soul, with each source retaining its own standing as further life proceeds from it. Compare that account with the compilation’s concern for transcendence and emanation. His sequence of principles is a distinct philosophical system; the resemblance does not identify those principles with the Bahá’í Manifestations or settle the arguments about Sufi unity.

subjects.displayTitle: The life of the spirit: becoming a source of life
subjects.introduction: A soul in which the spirit lives brings forth good fruit and becomes a divine tree. Spiritual life, in ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s account, is known by what it does: service, praiseworthy character, joy, and the power to bring hope to others. Bahá’u’lláh describes it as a life not of the flesh but of the spirit, possessed by those who have drunk from the ocean of faith and crowned by immortality, so that the believer lives in this world and the next. Life and death often name conditions rather than events; when Christ raised the dead, the dead received everlasting life, and those with a human spirit but no spirit of faith are counted dead though they walk. Water, light, breath, fire and wine approach the same renewal from different sides, and letters of consolation apply it to particular losses and martyrdoms. In John, the difficulty of Jesus’ words forces the disciples to decide where the words of eternal life are found [1]. The journey continues toward the second birth, the spirit of faith that distinguishes human from animal life, and the living waters that sustain it.
subjects.arc: Begin with spiritual fruit and service, explore the images of renewal, and read eternal life in relation to present conduct and particular losses.

order.why: Read the Book of Certitude’s account of a life beyond death.
shortened: Wert thou to attain to but a dewdrop of the crystal waters of divine knowledge, thou wouldst readily realize that true life is not the life of the flesh but the life of the spirit. For the life of the flesh is common to both men and animals, whereas the life of the spirit is possessed only by the pure in heart who have quaffed from the ocean of faith and partaken of the fruit of certitude. This life knoweth no death, and this existence is crowned by immortality.

order.why: Open with the reported tree bearing good fruit.
Give spiritual life a reported foundation in service and virtues.
shortened: Man becomes human only through spiritual life, and the foundation of such a life is made up of heavenly perfections, divine attributes, service to humanity, eagerness to receive eternal bounties, praiseworthy morals, unity, love of God, wisdom and knowledge of God.

order.why: Explains spiritual life through nearness to God and divine virtues.
Read the call to leave an enduring trace through good works.
Consider the cultivation of praiseworthy qualities.
Hear the reported relation between divine characteristics and spiritual life.
Establish the distinction between bodily and spiritual life.
shortened: Now, life is of two kinds: that of the body and that of the spirit. The life of the body consists in material life, but the life of the spirit is a heavenly existence which consists in receiving the grace of the Divine Spirit and being quickened through the breath of the Holy Spirit.

order.why: Consider the interpretation of scriptural healing and resurrection.
shortened: Consider that Christ reckoned as dead those who were nonetheless outwardly and physically alive; for true life is life eternal and true existence is spiritual existence. Thus if the Sacred Scriptures speak of raising the dead, the meaning is that they attained everlasting life; if they say that one who was blind was made to see, the meaning of this seeing is true insight; if they say that one who was deaf was made to hear, the meaning is that he acquired an inner ear and attained spiritual hearing.

order.why: Read Christ’s teachings as life-giving grace.
Keep the reported distinctions between human spirit and spirit of faith.
shortened: Let him whose is dead bury their dead, for those souls who have not believed in God, though they possess a human spirit, are deprived of the true spirit of faith and are therefore counted as dead. Though they have earthly life, they are bereft of heavenly life. The Prophets were sent to quicken this human spirit with the divine spirit. This is the spirit that causes the unity of the human world, the spirit that bestows eternal life, the spirit that confers everlasting felicity, the spirit that enables entry into the Kingdom of God, the spirit that transforms the earthly human into a divine being, the spirit that makes the terrestrial celestial, the spirit that changes darkness into light.

order.why: Read the relative use of death beside continuing awareness.
shortened: Those souls who are not vivified and attracted by the Holy Spirit, are accounted among the dead, because their souls are deprived of the Breath of the Holy Spirit, and these persons after physical death are in a certain condition, having feeling and discernment in their environment, but in comparison with the pure souls who have been vivified by the Holy Spirit, they are as dead and deprived.

order.why: Retain the reported judgment on material preoccupation in its historical context.
shortened: Especially in these countries which are exceedingly prosperous - in truth it is like a beehive. All are immersed in materialism.
All are bereft of the outpourings of the Holy Spirit and are heedless and deprived of eternal life.

order.why: Keep the forceful statement of deprivation within its spiritual imagery.
Read the invitation to drink from the heavenly river.
Consider the same life-giving water described as fire and light.
Hear the fragrance of holiness as a source of new life.
Read the invitation to receive that spiritual fragrance.
Follow the prayer’s images of water, fire, wine and mercy.
shortened: Some people among the companions of the right hand have discovered the manifest Light, have drunk from flowing waters, have quaffed from the fountain of certitude, have been guided to Thy straight path, have cast off restraint in their love for Thee among the sincere ones, and have been set ablaze with the fire of Thy love that quickeneth even old bones. The breeze of Thy tender mercy hath wafted over them, the pure wine of Thy bounty hath intoxicated them, and the attraction of Thy radiant beauty hath seized them.

order.why: Respond to the gifts of life and guidance through gratitude.
shortened: How can we render thanks that He brought us into being from nothingness, bestowed the spirit of existence upon us when we were utter void, granted us divine manifestation when we were sheer nothingness, guided us to the fountain of life when we were thirsting, clothed us in the garment of "Blessed be God, the Best of Creators" when we were naked, gave us direction when we were wandering, led us to His shelter when we were lost, granted seeing eyes when we were blind, bestowed hearing when we were deaf, gave us eternal life when we were dead, and granted spiritual freshness and grace when we were withered.

order.why: Read the lamp, tree, garment and cup as images of renewal.
Consider love illuminating the heart and human form.
shortened: O thou who hast obtained guidance from the light of the truth! The human temple is like unto a niche, and the heart is like unto a glass globe, and the love of God is like unto the light within that glass. When that lamp is ignited, the globe becometh illumined and the physical niche also becomes full of light and brilliance.

order.why: Read the relation of faith, lamp and niche.
shortened: O thou who art radiant with the lights of faith and dawning-place of the signs of certitude!

The heart is like a niche, and faith is like the lamp, and the pillars are like the glass globes. When these lights are kindled in this niche, it becomes a rose garden, and the lights of divine outpourings become manifest and radiant through these glass globes.

order.why: Follow guidance as its light reaches the senses and faculties.
shortened: O thou who art illumined by the light of divine guidance!

When the candle of guidance is kindled within the glass of the heart, it dispels the darkness of error that stems from worldly limitations. The lights of sanctification and the rays of unity shine upon all parts and members, senses and faculties.

order.why: Hear the prayer for nurture, maturity and spiritual revival.
shortened: I pray God to illumine thy heart with the light of the Manifestation, to nurture thee in His mercy so that thou mayest attain maturity in His love; thy spirit be enlightened with beholding His light and thy spirit revived by the bounty of the Holy Spirit, so that thou mayest be a sign of the love of God, speaking in the name of God, joyous by the favors of God, attaining unto the sea of the mercy of God, and being baptized with the water of life, the fire of love and the spirit of attraction.

order.why: Consider the practices that sustain spiritual life.
shortened: O thou maidservant of God! The physical life is sustained by respiration, eating of food and drinking of water; but the spiritual life consists of the mentioning of the True One, the Love of God, the explanation of the Knowledge of God and attraction to the Beauty of Abha. This is Everlasting Life. This is eternal Spirituality and this is Effulgence of His Highness the True One in the hearts of Humanity!

order.why: Read remembrance in earthly life and beyond.
Connect service and spiritual happiness.
Consider music and a new song as means of bringing joy.
Read the letter’s experience of a gathering enlivened by teachings.
shortened: O daughter of the Kingdom! Your letter was received and it indicated that you attended the Convention and witnessed the radiant lights of the divine teachings in that gathering, and saw souls brought to life with the spirit of eternal life.

order.why: Widen the image to a spirit animating the world’s body.
shortened: And the Blessed Cause and effects of the Most Great Manifestation are like the spirit of life in this mighty body and the most upright, greatest magnet. If the world and universe were not alive through this spirit, which is the qualities and perfections of the Beloved and the Most Merciful Lord, and were not freshened by these divine breaths, it would have the state of a dead body and the condition of a motionless corpse and carcass.

order.why: Keep the reported emphasis on care for others and inward qualities.
Hear the reported relation of spiritual life to happiness.
shortened: As for the spiritual perfections they are man's birthright and belong to him alone of all creation. Man is, in reality, a spiritual being, and only when he lives in the spirit is he truly happy.

order.why: Read the invitation toward joy in love and inspiration.
Consider the counsel to seek peace of conscience.
Hear the brief reported assurance of enduring happiness.
Read the reported relation of merciful feeling to lasting joy.
shortened: But if he possesses merciful susceptibilities, and if he is quickened with the divine spirit and if he realizes that he has attained to the eternal life - then these things will confer upon him a happiness which shall last throughout eternity.

order.why: Keep the personal reported desire for another’s spiritual happiness.
Read the appeal for an awakened and responsive heart.
Preserve the distinct devotional address to the lover.
Hear the prayer for increasing spiritual gladness.
Compare the three reported paths toward spiritual happiness.
Read humility as a way toward spiritual elevation.
shortened: Be lowly, that you may become noble. Be humble, that you may become as a rising star. Become effaced and evanescent, that you may find the ecstasy of the eternal wine.

order.why: Keep the blessing in the language of tribulation and love.
shortened: Blessed art thou for becoming intoxicated with the cup of tribulation and enkindled with the fire of the love of God.

order.why: Read the concern for lives whose opportunities have been constrained.
shortened: As to those souls who are born into this life as ethereal and radiant entities and yet, on account of their handicaps and trials, are deprived of great and real advantages, and leave the world without having lived to the full -- certainly this is a cause for grieving. This is the reason why the universal Manifestations of God unveil Their countenances to man, and endure every calamity and sore affliction, and lay down Their lives as a ransom; it is to make these very people, the ready ones, the ones who have capacity, to become dawning points of light, and to bestow upon them the life that fadeth never.

order.why: Consider the consolation concerning the fruit of a shortened life.
shortened: The length of life has no importance - what matters is salvation. Praise be to God, he has attained the fruit of life in the Kingdom of the All-Merciful, for the purpose of physical life is spiritual life and eternal existence in the divine realm. That gift has been secured and that noble quality established.

order.why: Keep the assurance addressed to a mother who has suffered loss.
shortened: The ultimate truth is that physical life was transformed into divine life, metaphorical existence was changed into true existence. You will find those radiant faces in the divine rose garden, you will see those incomparable saplings by the divine stream.

order.why: Read the consolation addressed to the widow of a martyred husband.
shortened: That was not death, it was life. It was not annihilation, it was existence itself. It was not calamity, it was divine grace.
This world will become a paradise, this world will be seen as heavenly, and the station of these souls will become apparent and known.

order.why: Consider the longing of the heavenly essence.
shortened: O heavenly friends! Earthly life is something that becomes contaminated with the impurities of this world, while the heavenly essence seeks the comfort of that eternal world.

order.why: Hear the reported distinction of spiritual longevity from physical duration.
Hear the promise of enduring vision and reunion.
shortened: The souls of the believers and the loved ones of God will attain, through the requisite of the spiritual world, everlasting vision and eternal reunion.

order.why: Read the reported upward journey of a spiritually reborn soul.
shortened: Every soul who is spiritually born - through the assistance of the Holy-Spirit - that soul which receives the Breath of the Holy Spirit will have an upward journey and attain to a lofty station in the spiritual world.

order.why: Consider the reported ship bearing souls toward immortal worlds.
shortened: God be praised that now you are on a Ship bearing you to immortal worlds. Day by day your signs will become clearer.

order.why: Read spiritual nearness despite physical distance.
Hear the acknowledgment of faith and certitude.
Keep the contrast of deprivation and renewed life in its addressed setting.
shortened: They are destitute; ye enjoy intimate access to the inmost secrets. They are counted as among the dead; ye are quickened and set free by the water of life, have become manifestations of divine favours, daysprings of guidance and centres of bestowals.

order.why: Close with the destiny attributed to the true believer.

questions: What fruits of spiritual life do these passages invite you to notice or cultivate?
How do water, light, breath, and a fruitful tree convey different aspects of renewal?
What changes when life and death are read as spiritual conditions rather than only bodily events?
How should the letters of consolation be approached with attention to the particular losses they address?
What does the disciples’ response in John add to the connection between understanding and receiving life?
How might remembrance, service, learning, or creative expression help you become a source of life to others?

references.label: 1 · John 6:60–69 · Words of spirit and life
references.note: Jesus speaks of the Spirit giving life, and the disciples confront the difficulty of his teaching. Peter responds by recognizing in Jesus the words of eternal life. Compare the relation between life, recognition, and response with the compilation’s interpretations of Christ. John’s narrative centers on commitment to Jesus; reading it alongside the Bahá’í passages invites comparison while retaining that specific setting.

subjects.displayTitle: Universal love: affinity, freedom, and responsibility
subjects.introduction: The force that keeps atoms clinging together in a stone, the pull that draws water up into a plant, the fellowship of animals and the yearning of a human heart: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá reads them all as one law appearing in rising degrees, and He gives that law its oldest name, love. Where attraction holds, there is composition and life; where it fails, there is separation and death. The human body makes the point concrete, its diverse members each needing all the others and held in order by a mind that is never seen but is known by its effects, and the universe itself is pictured as answering to a similar unifying power. The same Writings insist that everything in nature is its captive, except the human being, who can choose, and who is therefore answerable for whether love is spread. The Mettā Sutta trains that choice, wishing well to beings near and far, seen and unseen [1]. From here the path continues into interconnectedness and the chain of being, into diversity as a requirement of existence, and into the relation between nature and the will of God.
subjects.arc: Begin with the different expressions of love, examine order and interdependence, and return to the human responsibility for conscious unity.

order.why: Open with the Tablet of Love’s expansive account of a life-giving bond.
shortened: Love is the cause of God's revelation unto man, the vital bond inherent, in accordance with the divine creation, in the realities of things. Love is the one means that ensureth true felicity both in this world and the next. Love is the light that guideth in darkness, the living link that uniteth God with man, that assureth the progress of every illumined soul. Love is the most great law that ruleth this mighty and heavenly cycle, the unique power that bindeth together the divers elements of this material world, the supreme magnetic force that directeth the movements of the spheres in the celestial realms.

order.why: Distinguish love’s expressions in different kingdoms.
Hear the reported description of magnetism as a symbol.
Establish the need for sensible images when speaking of spiritual realities.
Read attraction in relation to differing stations.
shortened: For the variation in the stations of love are from differences of stations and stages and in each world of the worlds and in each stage of the stages there can be seen a magnetism of oneness .  Within the grasp of its power is the mutual attraction of the reality of all things and the pulling [together] of the subtlety of Being.  And this magnetism of oneness is the station of Love and Attraction (khullat ).

order.why: Follow the account from elemental connection to human yearning.
shortened: O thou who art yearning to discover! The discoverers of the mysteries of existence and those who comprehend the qualities and hidden secrets hold that a wondrous force of attraction and a strange magnetic power of connection permeates and encompasses all these infinite beings and successive contingent things, both physical and spiritual, and is equally present in them all.

In truth, every thing has unveiled itself through that universal attractive force with a manifestation and light and has displayed its beauty. And in human reality it has become the power of yearning, bringing about enthusiasm and passion and attraction.

order.why: Examine the reported progression through mineral, vegetable and animal affinity.
shortened: The power of cohesion expressed in the mineral kingdom is in reality love or affinity manifested in a low degree according to the exigencies of the mineral world. We take a step higher into the vegetable kingdom where we find an increased power of attraction has become manifest among the composing elements which form phenomena. Through this degree of attraction a cellular admixture is produced among these elements which make up the body of a plant. Therefore, in the degree of the vegetable kingdom there is love. We enter the animal kingdom and find the attractive power binding together single elements as in the mineral, plus the cellular admixture as in the vegetable, plus the phenomena of feelings or susceptibilities. We observe that the animals are susceptible to certain affiliation and fellowship and that they exercise natural selection. This elemental attraction, this admixture and selective affinity is love manifest in the degree of the animal kingdom.

order.why: Read the reported contrast of composition and separation.
shortened: When we observe the phenomena of the universe, we realize that the axis around which life revolves is love, while the axis around which death and destruction revolve is animosity and hatred. Let us view the mineral kingdom. Here we see that if attraction did not exist between the atoms, the composite substance of matter would not be possible.
The proof is clear that in all degrees and kingdoms unity and agreement, love and fellowship are the cause of life, whereas dissension, animosity and separation are ever conducive to death.

order.why: Consider the reported examples of wood and stone.
Hear the reported relation of affinity to the possibility of life.
shortened: If the atoms which compose the kingdom of the minerals were without affinity for each other, the earth would never have been formed, the universe could not have been created. Because they have affinity for each other, the power of life is able to manifest itself, and the organisms of the phenomenal world become possible.

order.why: Read the reported account of cohesion.
shortened: In the Universe, all atoms and particles are united by the power of attraction and cohesion; if it were not for this, everything would be immediately dissolved and annihilated.

order.why: Keep the reported identification of attraction with love.
shortened: All things in existence are formed by particles and atoms which are united by the power of attraction. This is such a great power that all the world is held together by it - and not only the world, but the Universe. All are made of atoms and united by attraction. What is this power of attraction? Love!

order.why: Consider the reported image of the motion of spheres.
shortened: Even these massive spheres revolve through the force of attraction, the force of love. Love bestows wondrous life upon lifeless bodies.

order.why: Read the reported description of creation as an expression of love.
shortened: Everything partakes of this nature and is subject to this principle, for the creative foundation in all its degrees and kingdoms is an expression or outcome of love.

order.why: Hear the reported contrast between affinity and discord.
Examine the Forel Tablet’s relationships and all-unifying agency.
shortened: And though these infinite realities are diverse in their character yet they are in the utmost harmony and closely connected together. As one's vision is broadened and the matter observed carefully, it will be made certain that every reality is but an essential requisite of other realities. Thus to connect and harmonize these diverse and infinite realities an all-unifying Power is necessary, that every part of existent being may in perfect order discharge its own function. Consider the body of man, and let the part be an indication of the whole.

It is the mind that is the all-unifying agency that so uniteth all the component parts one with the other that each dischargeth its specific function in perfect order, and thereby co-operation and reaction are made possible.

order.why: Read the argument for a universal directing power.
shortened: Likewise, look into this endless universe: a universal power inevitably existeth, which encompasseth all, directing and regulating all the parts of this infinite creation; and were it not for this Director, this Co-ordinator, the universe would be flawed and deficient. It would be even as a madman; whereas ye can see that this endless creation carrieth out its functions in perfect order, every separate part of it performing its own task with complete reliability, nor is there any flaw to be found in all its workings. Thus it is clear that a Universal Power existeth, directing and regulating this infinite universe.

order.why: Consider motion and attraction in the Tablet of the Celestial Spheres.
Read nature as governed by one order.
Consider the relation of development to universal law.
Read the analogy between particular and universal existence.
shortened: Universal existences can be likened and compared to particular ones, for both are subject to one natural order, one universal law, and one divine arrangement. For instance, you will find the smallest atoms to be similar in their general structure to the greatest entities in the universe, and it is clear that they have proceeded from one laboratory of might according to one natural order and one universal law, and can therefore be compared to one another.

order.why: Hear the reported chain in which every link affects the order.
Consider the reported range of beings under universal law.
Keep the reported statement about the fixed channel of natural law.
Read the sun and ocean as subject to natural order.
Consider the sea and sun in the comparison with human comprehension.
Hear the reported account of celestial bodies under law.
Read the reported distinction of humanity within nature.
Consider the reported list of natural beings and the human exception.
Hear the extended reported argument about human capacities.
shortened: Observe that all beings, whether great or small, are captives of nature. For example, the sun with all its grandeur is captive to nature. All planets, all brilliant stars are captive to nature. All natures, all elements are captive to nature. All minerals, all plants, all animals are captives of nature. They cannot transgress, and none can deviate from nature's requirements even by an atom's worth.
None can make the slightest transgression from nature's rule and law except humans, who are rulers over nature.

order.why: Keep the reported statement about the limits of created things.
Read the reported example of animal behavior.
Consider the reported contrast of grandeur with volition.
Keep the human body itself within nature.
shortened: The body of man is a prisoner of nature and will act in accordance with whatsoever nature dictates.

order.why: Read the limits that also constrain humanity.
shortened: It is certain that the entire contingent world is subject to an order and a law which it can never disobey. Even man is forced to submit to death, sleep, and other conditions-that is, in certain matters he is compelled, and this very compulsion implies the existence of One Who is All-Compelling.

order.why: Consider the reported claim of human conquest of nature.
Read the reported dependence of that capacity on spiritual power.
shortened: On all sides he is surrounded by dangers and difficulties, against which his physical body alone cannot cope. If a man looks at the world around him, he will see how all created things are dependent and are captive to the laws of Nature.
Man alone, by his spiritual power, has been able to free himself, to soar above the world of matter and to make it his servant.

order.why: Turn to the problem of uniting different human understandings.
shortened: It is clear that human realities differ one from another, that opinions and perceptions vary, and that this divergence of thoughts, opinions, understandings and sentiments among individuals is an essential requirement. For differences of degree in creation are among the essential requirements of existence, which is resolved into countless forms. We stand therefore in need of a universal power which can prevail over the thoughts, opinions and sentiments of all, which can annul these divisions and bring all souls under the sway of the principle of the oneness of humanity. And it is clear and evident that the greatest power in the human world is the love of God.

order.why: Consider the invitation to bring human systems into harmonious order.
Hear the reported relation of divine law to truth, reason and justice.
shortened: 'The Laws of God are not imposition of will, or of power, or pleasure, but the resolutions of truth, reason and justice.'

order.why: Keep the statement concerning love’s development within its addressed context.
Read the reported call to spread love throughout humanity.
shortened: The first sign of faith is love. The message of the holy, divine Manifestations is love; the phenomena of creation are based upon love; the radiance of the world is due to love; the well-being and happiness of the world depend upon it. Therefore, I admonish you that you must strive throughout the human world to diffuse the light of love.

order.why: Close the linked passages with the reported praise of love’s power.
shortened: What a power is love! It is the most wonderful, the greatest of all living powers.
In the world of existence there is indeed no greater power than the power of love.

order.why: Describes universal love as a magnet that attracts realities and diffuses life.
Retain the supplied account of a dynamic harmony of religion and science.
Close with the supplied image of discovering and cooperating with law.

questions: What different senses of love appear as the passages move from matter to human relationships?
How does the image of an interconnected body help explain unity that includes distinct functions?
Where can analogies from nature illuminate human conduct, and where do they need limits?
How do the passages hold human freedom together with dependence on natural conditions?
What does the Buddhist practice of goodwill toward all beings add to the idea of universal connection?
What daily choice might express a more conscious responsibility for the relationships that sustain your life?

references.label: 1 · Karaṇīya Mettā Sutta, Sutta Nipāta 1.8 · A heart without exclusion
references.note: In Thanissaro Bhikkhu’s translation, the practitioner cultivates goodwill toward beings of every kind and in every direction, without wishing suffering upon another. Compare this deliberate training of care with the compilation’s invitation to spread love. The sutta offers an ethical and contemplative practice within a Buddhist path to liberation; it does not present love as the physical force binding the universe or as an argument about a Creator.

subjects.displayTitle: The state of prayer: attention, communion, and action
subjects.introduction: Why speak to God at all, when He already knows every wish of the heart? ‘Abdu’l-Bahá answers with the simplest of analogies: a friend who loves another will want to say so, and will look for every chance to speak, to bring gifts, to write. Prayer is that impulse, conversation with the Beloved. Yet the conversation has an inner discipline. Words matter less than the soul’s condition; the mind can become an altar and the heart a sanctuary, so that one lives in a continuing attitude of prayer. The Báb adds that the supplicant must behold nothing but the face of his Lord, and that whoever prays for a need should also seek its means, since God works through channels. Prayers that seem unanswered are met not with blame but with the language of wisdom and surrender. Paul’s picture of the Spirit interceding when we do not know how to pray offers a kindred sense of help amid limitation [1]. From here the path leads into meditation, the law of obligatory prayer, and the real power of prayer in a life.
subjects.arc: Begin with communion and love, explore attention and receptivity, distinguish forms of prayer, and end with surrender joined to action.

order.why: Hear the sweetness of intimate prayer.
shortened: There is a pleasure in offering prayers that transcends all other pleasures, and there is a sweetness in chanting and singing the verses of God which is the greatest desire of all the believers, men and women alike. While reciting the Obligatory Prayer, one converses intimately and shares secrets with the true Beloved. No pleasure is greater than this, if one proceeds with a detached soul, with tears overflowing, with a trusting heart and an eager spirit. Every joy is earthly save this one, the sweetness of which is divine.

order.why: Open with the reported experience of prayer as conversation.
shortened: What is prayer? It is 'conversation with God.' While man prays he sees himself in the Presence of God. If he concentrates his attention he will surely at the time of Prayer realize that he is 'conversing with God.'

order.why: Consider the reported wish to speak even when love is already known.
shortened: "If one friend feels love for another he will wish to say so. Though he knows that the first is aware that he loves him, he will still wish to say so. If there is anyone that you love do you not seek an opportunity to speak with him, to speak lovingly with him, to bring him gifts, to write him letters? If you do not feel such a desire it would be that you did not love your friend. God knows the wishes of all hearts. But the impulse to pray is a natural one springing from man's love to God.

order.why: Read obligatory prayer through the desire for companionship.
shortened: The wisdom of obligatory prayer is this: That it causeth a connection between the servant and the True One, because at that time man with all his heart and soul turneth his face towards the Almighty, seeking His association and desiring His love and companionship. For a lover, there is no greater pleasure than to converse with his beloved, and for a seeker, there is no greater bounty than intimacy with the object of his desire.

order.why: Examine supplication as itself a light and an enlargement of capacity.
shortened: When one supplicates to his Lord, turns unto Him and seeks Bounty from His Ocean, this supplication is by itself a light to his heart, an illumination to his sight, a life to his soul and an exaltation for his being.

When the vessel is widened the water increaseth, and when the thirst grows the bounty of the cloud becomes agreeable to the taste of man. This is the mystery of supplication and the wisdom of stating one's wants (praying).

order.why: Read prayer as water of life.
shortened: O thou daughter of the Kingdom!  Know thou that supplication and prayer is the Water of Life.  It is the cause of the vivification of existence, and endows glad-tidings and joy to the souls.

order.why: Hear the brief reported effect on the heart.
Keep the reported praise of the state of prayer.
Consider the reported relationship of words and attitude.
Read the personal report concerning wordless prayer and its explicit distinction from obligatory prayer.
Carry the reported attitude of prayer into continuing life.
Hear the prayer that reaches beyond words and sounds.
shortened: Reveal then Thyself, O Lord! by Thy merciful Utterance and the mystery of Thy Divine Being, that the holy ecstasy of prayer may fill our souls -- a prayer that shall rise above words and letters and transcend the murmur of syllables and sounds -- that all things may be merged into nothingness before the revelation of Thy Splendour.

order.why: Keep the voice of a supplicant with a wandering heart.
shortened: O my God, my God! Thou hearest my crying in the depths of night and my wailing in the morning and evening hours. I supplicate Thee during my prayer and devotions with a wandering heart and flowing tears and a throbbing breast.

order.why: Read dependence and appeal for assistance.
shortened: It is incumbent upon every servant to pray and supplicate God, and to beg for and implore His assistance! This is the attitude of a true worshipper (devotee) and thy Lord is able to perform whatsoever He wishes through His excellent wisdom.

order.why: Consider humility and the request for confirmation.
shortened: O friends! Recite this prayer with utmost humility and supplication at the Threshold of the King of the Kingdom of Glory, and seek confirmation.

order.why: Read the invitation to midnight communion.
shortened: O seeker of Truth!
If thou desirest that God may open thine eye, thou must supplicate unto God, pray to and commune with Him at midnight, saying:
O Lord, I have turned my face unto Thy kingdom of oneness and am immersed in the sea of Thy mercy.

order.why: Hear the reported counsel to Lua Getsinger concerning fervent prayer.
shortened: In the middle of nights pray and supplicate to God with such fervor and zeal that I may hear thy calls.'"

order.why: Attend to the present hour of supplication.
Read continued prayer in relation to steadfastness and joy.
Consider the reported conditions of attention and surrender.
shortened: Man is eternally in a state of communion and prayer with the source of all-good. The highest and most elevating state is the state of prayer. Prayer is communion with God ... Its efficacy is conditioned upon the freedom of the heart from extraneous suggestions and mundane thoughts. The worshipper must pray with a detached spirit, unconditional surrender of the will, concentrated attention and a magnetic spiritual passion. His innermost being must be stirred with the ethereal breezes of sanctification.

order.why: Keep the reported counsel about distractions.
Read the historical report of restrained public expression and inward love.
shortened: If you see some of the people here in Haifa not paying their entire attention to prayer, it is because they are afraid of causing an uproar in the Government. When a man falls in love with a human being, it is impossible for him to keep from mentioning the name of his beloved. How much more difficult is it to keep from mentioning the name of GOD, when he has come to love Him.

order.why: Examine the Báb’s account of unity and prayer as its own answer.
shortened: It behooves the supplicant to behold none but the countenance of his Lord at the time of prayer, for if he finds himself or his desire while turning to his Lord, he has associated partners with his Master and has not truly turned in the station of prayer.

For this reason, God does not accept the prayers of most supplicants, nor are they answered, because they call upon what they do not know. When anyone calls upon God in this way, God answers immediately, for turning to God in true unity is greater than what the servant asks of his Lord. Prayer in that station is itself the answer, and therefore God has said: "Call upon Me; I will answer you."

order.why: Consider the limits of particular requests and the language of wisdom.
shortened: O handmaid of God! Prayers are granted through the universal Manifestations of God.

If healing is right for the patient, it will certainly be granted; but for some ailing persons, healing would only be the cause of other ills, and therefore wisdom doth not permit an affirmative answer to the prayer.

order.why: Read the Báb’s counsel to seek the means of fulfillment.
shortened: Verily God createth all things through their means, and He causeth all means to flow through their channels. When thou prayest to God for any need, look unto its means and seek to attract it through its means, for God will grant thee this, albeit through its means. Look not unto the means nor the cause, but rather unto the Causer of causes, Who operateth not through means but Who causeth the means to operate through their channels.

order.why: Hear the prayer to speak the divine name and act on its commandments.
Introduce the distinction concerning prescribed congregational prayer.
Read the reported distinction between personal obligatory prayer and public supplication.
Describes concentration, purity and self-forgetfulness in obligatory prayer.
Consider the reported value of gathering to pray.
Keep the reported reflection on individual prayer in its particular terms.
Read the relation of observance and humility.
shortened: Prayer without ablution is impossible, and supplication without humility is unacceptable.

order.why: Consider the words accompanying the washing of the face.
shortened: And while washing his face, let him say:
I have turned my face unto Thee, O my Lord! Illumine it with the light of Thy countenance. Protect it, then, from turning to any one but Thee.

order.why: Keep the particular letter’s guidance about prayer and its times.
shortened: However, firstly, one should perform it whenever one finds in oneself a state of devotion and humility; secondly, in the morning, at noon, and in the evening; and thirdly, from noon to noon."

order.why: Retain the reported question about dawn prayer and ablution.
Read obligatory prayer through complete devotion.
shortened: O My brother! How great, how very great, can the law of obligatory prayer be, when, through His mercy and loving kindness, one is enabled to observe it. When a man commenceth the recitation of the Obligatory Prayer, he should see himself severed from all created things and regard himself as utter nothingness before the will and purpose of God, in such wise that he seeth naught but Him in the world of being.

order.why: Consider the direction of attention toward Bahá’u’lláh.
shortened: During the time of prayer His Holiness Baha’u’llah must be singly and alone the center towards whom all the faces are turned.

order.why: Hear the reported personal practice of turning toward the Blessed Perfection.
Keep the reported counsel concerning an object of concentration.
Read the reported distinction of attributes from personality.
shortened: Abdul-Baha said:
"If we wish to pray we must have some object upon which to concentrate. If we turn to God we must direct our hearts to a certain center.
"The epitome of all worship is the worship of the attributes of Christ, not his personality."

order.why: Preserve the distinct prayer concerning healing and religious practice.
Read the Báb’s quotation of a tradition about moderated recitation.
Hear the Báb’s particular counsel concerning reading verses.
shortened: When ye tire of reading a verse from the Book of God a hundred times, then reduce it by ten and ten until there remaineth but nineteen. This sufficeth you before your Lord in the paths of goodness, if ye be of them that wish to act. Say: Ye draw not nigh unto God by aught as ye do by reading His verses by night and by day, whether ye read them silently within yourselves or proclaim them aloud with your tongues.

order.why: Close the linked passages with the reported daily relation of love, work, prayer, peace and joy.
Retain the supplied guidance about prayer to God and through the Manifestation.
Consider the supplied image of the door to knowing God.
Read the supplied guidance that preserves the words of revealed prayers.
Keep flexibility of thought together with distinctions of station.
shortened: In regard to your question: we must not be rigid about praying; there is not a set of rules governing it; the main thing is we must start out with the right concept of God, the Manifestation, the Master, the Guardian -- we can turn, in thought, to any one of them when we pray.
As long as you don't confuse their stations, and make them all equal, it does not matter much how you orient your thoughts.

order.why: Consider the supplied movement from a visual image toward qualities.
Read the supplied provisional description of worship in unity.
Compare the supplied Dionysian account of drawing nearer through prayer.
Keep the supplied distinction concerning singing in a gathering.
Read the fuller supplied explanation of collective recitation and ritual.
shortened: There is a difference between chanting a prayer collectively and congregational prayer. The latter is a formal prayer usually led by an individual using a prescribed ritual. Congregational prayer in this form is forbidden in the Faith except in the case of the Prayer for the Dead.

order.why: Consider the supplied counsel addressed to disappointment and suffering.
shortened: Although you seem to feel that your prayers have not so far been answered, and do no longer have any hope that your material conditions will ameliorate, the Guardian wishes you nevertheless not to allow such disappointments to undermine your faith in the power of prayer, but rather to continue entreating the Almighty to enable you to discover the great wisdom which may be hidden behind all these sufferings.

The true worshipper, while praying, should endeavour not so much to ask God to fulfill his wishes and desires, but rather to adjust these and make them conform to the Divine Will. Only through such an attitude can one derive that feeling of inner peace and contentment which the power of prayer alone can confer.

order.why: Close with the supplied relation of meditation, supplication and action.
shortened: The true basis of prayer is for the individual to hold himself as a reed, through which the Holy Spirit may flow. His will should be completely submissive to the Will of God.

The Guardian has so often pointed out that there are three elements of prayer -- meditation, supplication and action. It is most important that an individual act, because it is only while the individual is acting that a prayer can be answered.

questions: What does the image of conversation with a beloved illuminate about prayer?
How do words, silence, attention, and bodily observance contribute differently to the practice described here?
What distinctions help reconcile individual obligatory prayer with gathering or reciting together?
How might seeking practical means become part of a prayerful response to a need?
What does Paul’s account of prayer beyond words add to the passages about limited understanding and surrender?
How could a continuing attitude of prayer influence your work, relationships, or response to disappointment?

references.label: 1 · Romans 8:26–27 · Prayer when words and understanding fail
references.note: Paul describes the Spirit helping human weakness and interceding when people do not know how to pray, in accordance with God’s will. Compare this with the compilation’s prayer beyond syllables and its concern to orient desire toward divine wisdom. Paul’s account has a specifically Christian understanding of the Spirit and intercession; its point of comparison is assistance and receptivity amid human limitation.
